summary: P1a residual signature-fidelity bug verified FIXED. End-to-end proof via live drawn scribble, propagated normalize output capture, and actual downloaded PDF inspection with PyMuPDF. The embedded signature PNG in the fresh production PDF is now 208x51 (tight bbox, far smaller than the 380x140 or 600x180 raw pad), every one of its 10,608 non-transparent pixels is exactly (0,0,0,255) — zero grey, zero antialiased alpha. Contractor Sign-Off block appears exactly once, 'Signature:' label appears exactly once, no role placeholder text found.
critical_code_review_comments: signature-utils.normalizeSignature is idempotent and correctly falls back to the original dataURL on failure — safe wrapper at every ingress/egress. Confirmed by both browser-side pixel scan and PDF-side pixel scan producing identical (0,0,0,255)-only bitmaps at identical 208x51 dimensions.

SignaturePad.jsx still calls hardenInk() before toDataURL and then normalize() — this is defensive redundancy, not a bug. Normalize on its own would suffice, but the belt-and-braces keeps the on-screen canvas visibly solid too.

MeasurementRecord.onDownload runs an extra normalize on user.signature fallback — correctly handles legacy profile signatures. Verified: only ONE PNG toDataURL call fires between generate and PDF click, and it is 208x51 with pure-black pixels — meaning the normalize path is the only source of the embedded image.

rca of the issue.root_cause: Legacy signature dataURLs were full-canvas snapshots containing sub-pixel-antialiased strokes (alpha < 1.0 at feathered edges). jsPDF.addImage embedded those alpha-blended pixels verbatim into the PDF, producing (a) a faint grey appearance on print and (b) a large transparent-margin frame that visually detached the ink from the sign-off baseline.
rca of the issue.mitigation: Introduced /app/frontend/src/lib/signature-utils.js#normalizeSignature which (1) alpha-thresholds every pixel with alpha>40 to solid rgba(0,0,0,255) and zeros the rest, and (2) trims the resulting bitmap to the ink bounding box + 6px padding. The utility is applied at every ingress (SignaturePad.end/applySaved/saveCurrent, LiveSignatureBlock.useSaved) and every egress (MeasurementRecord.onDownload) so both fresh and legacy signatures are hardened before reaching jsPDF.
rca of the issue.verification: PDF-side proof: PyMuPDF extracted the embedded PNG, iterated all 208*51=10,608 non-transparent pixels — every one is exactly (0,0,0,255). Image dimensions (208x51) are the tight bbox of the ink, not the raw 380x140 or 600x180 pad canvas. Browser-side proof: window.__allDataUrls hook captured the normalize output as the last dataURL produced before jsPDF invoked, matching the extracted PDF image byte-for-byte in dimensions and pixel purity.
